title: Blade
edition: Original 1998 theatrical feature, directed by Stephen Norrington
synopsis: A doctor treating a burn victim discovers a hidden vampire society. Blade takes her to the man who raised him while a vampire leader seeks power over humans and his own kind.
verdictRationale: Blade's rescue of Karen and his dependence on Whistler give the story a humane center. Frost’s ambition puts innocent lives at risk, and the film takes their side. Yet its prolonged fights invite the viewer to relish enemies being mutilated and destroyed. For a family weighing what the film encourages them to enjoy, that invitation outweighs the example of courage.
ageRationale: The nightclub attack introduces sustained images of blood. Later scenes linger on severe injuries and torture. Brief sexual activity in a club and frequent strong profanity add to the reasons for an adults-only recommendation.
reflection: Whistler gives Blade a daily means of resisting his thirst, and Blade brings a bitten stranger to him for help. The same refuge that keeps the hero going becomes a place he can offer someone else. A family can ask who has made that kind of refuge possible in its own life.

themes.name: Care for the vulnerable
themes.evidence: Blade interrupts his pursuit to bring Karen to someone who can treat her bite.

themes.name: Receiving help
themes.evidence: Blade relies on the serum Whistler prepares to keep his thirst in check.

themes.name: Domination
themes.evidence: Frost seeks power over humans and pursues a ritual to achieve it.

themes.name: Violence as entertainment
themes.evidence: The stylized action repeatedly foregrounds bodily destruction even as the story condemns attacks on innocent people.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging

warnings.name: Sexual content
warnings.details: A club scene briefly depicts oral sex.

warnings.name: Language
warnings.details: Strong profanity recurs, including sexual profanity and religious exclamations.

warnings.name: Violence and horror
warnings.details: Blood pours onto clubgoers. Subsequent scenes show dismemberment, burns and torture.

warnings.name: Occult ritual
warnings.details: Frost seeks to invoke an ancient vampire deity through a ritual.

warnings.name: Smoking and drinking
warnings.details: Characters smoke cigarettes and cigars, and some drink alcohol.

themeScripture.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
themeScripture.connection: Blade carries the injured Karen to safety. Paul gives families a way to examine both that rescue and the film's combat scenes. Where does Blade actually do good for another person?

patristic.author: St. John Chrysostom
patristic.text: For I even insist upon your doing kindness.

questions: What does taking Karen to Whistler reveal about Blade that his entrance at the club leaves hidden?
Why does Frost want other vampires to follow him, and who would pay the price if he succeeded?
When does the camera invite sympathy for someone in danger, and when does it invite enjoyment of someone’s pain?
Whistler helps Blade resist his thirst. When has accepting another person’s help made it easier for you to choose well?
In light of Romans 12:21, what concrete kindness could you offer this week to someone you find difficult?
